# Sirach Chapter 32 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 32 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_032_page_001.jpg

---

32:1 Have you been put in charge of a dinner party? Don't let it go to your head. Treat your guests as equals, look after them properly, and then take your seat.

32:2 Once you've done your job, sit back and enjoy yourself — you've earned the honor that comes with doing it well.

32:3 If you're an elder, go ahead and speak — that's your prerogative. But show good judgment, and don't interrupt the music.

32:4 When entertainment is underway, don't monopolize the conversation. There's a time and place for showing off your wisdom, and this isn't it.

32:5 A well-played concert at a wine banquet is like a ruby set in gold.

32:6 Fine music alongside good wine is like an emerald seal mounted in a golden ring.

32:7 If you're young, speak only when you must — and even then, briefly, only when you've been asked more than once.

32:8 Get to the point. Say a lot with a few words. Show that you know when to speak and when to keep quiet.

32:9 Among your elders, don't act like their equal, and when someone else is talking, don't chime in uninvited.

32:10 Just as lightning comes before thunder, so a person of genuine character makes a good impression before they even open their mouth.

32:11 Leave in good time; don't be the last to go. Head straight home and don't wander.

32:12 Once home, do whatever your heart wants — just don't let your speech become arrogant.

32:13 Above all, thank your Creator, who has lavished his good things upon you.

32:14 Those who respect the Lord welcome his correction, and those who seek him earnestly will find his blessing.

32:15 Those who study God's instruction will be enriched by it, but the hypocrite will trip over it.

32:16 Those who fear the Lord find true direction, and their right actions shine like a lamp in the dark.

32:17 The sinner resents correction and always manages to find an excuse.

32:18 A wise person doesn't dismiss a nagging doubt, but a proud and reckless person barges ahead without fear.

32:19 Never act without thinking it through first — and once you've acted, don't second-guess yourself.

32:20 Don't take a road that's full of hazards, and don't stumble on rough ground.

32:21 Don't be overconfident about a road that looks easy, and watch out for your own impulses along the way.

32:22 Be careful in everything you do — that, too, is what keeping God's commandments means.

32:23 The person who obeys God's law protects themselves, and the person who trusts in the Lord will not be disappointed.

32:24 Nothing truly bad will happen to those who fear the Lord; when they are tested, God will rescue them time and again.
